solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scoundrel is embraced by dull person with fixed views

parts.note: a dog is an old word for a worthless rogue

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside, so the word is goes within the synonym for dull

parts.note: matt describes a surface without shine, so dull

explanation.surface: A rogue is being hugged by a boring, opinionated person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dull person' reads as one phrase, but 'dull' alone (matt) is wordplay; 'embraced by' puts IS inside MATT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dogmatic asserts opinions as unquestionable truths, so a person with rigidly fixed views fits.

clue.text: A batting failure for a famous Donald

definitions.meaning: in cricket, being out for zero runs is a nought

explanation.surface: A cricket flop credited to some well-known man named Donald.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter dismissed without scoring has made a duck; Donald is Disney's cartoon one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang names a zero score after the egg-shaped nought; Disney's Donald is a cartoon waterfowl.

clue.text: Huge fellow I look up in biblical city

indicators.note: the reversed letters are placed inside the name of the city

parts.note: Gath was a Philistine city in the Old Testament

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A big man looks up at the sky while standing in an Old Testament town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns I + LO into OLI, which goes 'in' GATH. Fittingly, the giant came from Gath.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine giant slain by David is the byword for an enormous man.

clue.text: Military ruler unaffected by revolution

definitions.note: an Ottoman commander's title, which reads the same in both directions

indicators.note: turning the word round leaves it exactly the same, a palindrome

parts.note: an Ottoman commander's title, which reads the same in both directions

explanation.surface: A general stays in power, untouched by the uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a coup but means turning the word backwards; the three letters read the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Ottoman Empire this title was given to a military commander or chief officer.

clue.text: Like a prisoner as part of a team

definitions.meaning: slang for being in jail, locked within

explanation.surface: A footballer feels jailed while playing for the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into IN SIDE, side being a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a convict is said to be locked away within; read as two words, it means playing for a side.

clue.text: Lessons? Disapproving remark before one enters tests!

indicators.note: the remark comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval

indicators.note: one entering means it goes inside the word for tests

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A teacher tuts as a pupil walks into the exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' puts I inside ORALS (spoken exams); 'before' sets TUT first.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-group teaching sessions, especially at university, are a kind of lesson.

clue.text: Place selling drinks in Prohibition

definitions.meaning: a ban, as in a ... on something

explanation.surface: A speakeasy pours drinks during the American Prohibition era.
explanation.walkthrough: Prohibition with a capital looks like the 1920s US alcohol ban, but here it simply means a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub is a place serving drinks, and a ban or barrier is also a bar.

clue.text: Dessert was a failure, lacking finishing touch

explanation.surface: A pudding flopped because it lacked a final garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking finishing touch' removes the last letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen moulded pudding, often of ice cream, is a classic French sweet course.

clue.text: Once again hand out book

definitions.meaning: to book is to make a reservation

explanation.surface: Someone redistributes a library volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as RE-SERVE: serve again.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in two parts it means dealing out a second time, and as one word it means to book in advance.

clue.text: Merchants said to be in these wine stores

indicators.note: the word for merchants is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: traders who sell goods are sellers

explanation.surface: Wine traders are supposedly found down among their stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' marks the sound-alike: SELLERS and CELLARS are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground storerooms are where bottles of vintage are traditionally kept.

clue.text: Periods that may be indicated with a cross

definitions.text: may be indicated with a cross
definitions.meaning: the multiplication sign is an x-shaped cross

explanation.surface: Some eras are marked on a calendar with an X.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross is the multiplication sign, read aloud as 'times'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras or spells are periods, and the x-shaped sign is said as this word in arithmetic.

clue.text: Any car dealer gets organised for a twelve-month period

indicators.note: the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A car salesman gets his affairs in order for the next year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets organised' rearranges ANY CAR DEALER.
explanation.definitionFit: January to December is the span of a year as reckoned on the calendar.

clue.text: Undemanding university post where one sits back and relaxes?

definitions.text: where one sits back and relaxes?

explanation.surface: A cushy professorship is a job where the holder can take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: A chair is a university professorship; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep upholstered armchair is furniture for lounging and resting in comfort.

clue.text: The fellow's in risky venture giving order

indicators.note: the fellow's goes inside the gamble

parts.note: he's is short for he is, the fellow is

explanation.surface: A man gambling on a venture is issuing commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks a container; 'giving' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A command or bidding, as in 'at his request', is an order.

clue.text: Journalist gets cleaner to go round part of the house

indicators.note: the cleaning tool surrounds the journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter hires a cleaner to do a circuit of the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' marks a container; 'cleaner' looks like a person but is a sweeping brush, and ED (editor) is the standard journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for sleeping is one area within a home.

clue.text: Puzzle created by regulating device

definitions.meaning: a plate or screen controlling flow of air, sound or water

explanation.surface: A mysterious mechanism leaves someone puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: To perplex someone is to puzzle them, and a plate that restrains the flow of air or sound is also so called.

clue.text: Life apt to be nasty in dingy, dirty building

indicators.note: turning nasty suggests the letters are made disorderly

explanation.surface: Living in a shabby run-down place is apt to be grim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be nasty' rearranges LIFE APT.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema or theatre, supposedly infested with insects.

clue.text: Electricity in stable

definitions.meaning: a charge built up on surfaces, as in crackling hair

explanation.surface: Power is being supplied to the horses' stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a horse building but is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge that builds up without flowing is called by this name, which also means not moving.

clue.text: Shop with decent sales I redeveloped

indicators.note: rebuilding something means rearranging it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper boasts of good takings after a refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' rearranges DECENT SALES I.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and fine prepared foods is a kind of store.

clue.text: Knowing sort of look — mystery's ending

parts.note: a leer is a sly or lecherous look

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A sly glance is given as a whodunnit reaches its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last letter of mystery's, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary and suspicious implies a knowing, distrustful attitude.

clue.text: River Don

definitions.meaning: a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland

explanation.surface: A river named after a Don.
explanation.walkthrough: The WEAR is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: A north-east English river shares its name with the verb for having clothes on, which is what don means.

clue.text: Last of the Athenian characters

parts.note: the final letter of the Greek alphabet, the letters used in Athens

explanation.surface: The last of the people in Athens are leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people but means letters of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet ends with this letter, the one after psi.

clue.text: Tramp unsettled a priest

indicators.note: disturbed, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A vagrant has upset a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges A PRIEST; 'Tramp' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge wearily from place to place is to tramp.

clue.text: Star not entirely graceful

indicators.note: only some of the word's letters are used, taken from within it

explanation.surface: A celebrity is somewhat less than elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' takes letters from inside graceful.
explanation.definitionFit: A top performer or expert is called a star or a crack player.

clue.text: Month mistaken as year, initially

indicators.note: the first letter of each of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone takes a month to be a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of mistaken, as, year.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth month of the calendar.

clue.text: See who Jane married

definitions.meaning: a bishop's diocese, here the Kent cathedral city
in Charlotte Bronte's novel Jane Eyre, the heroine weds her employer, Mr Edward Fairfax of Thornfield

explanation.surface: Look who Jane ended up wedding!
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese; Jane is Jane Eyre, whose 'Reader, I married him' refers to her employer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent diocese is one of England's oldest sees, and Brontë's Jane weds her employer of this surname.
